summary: LTP and Quote clients on one NSE equity: the Quote client moves the subscription up (a PUT of the LTP code, a POST of 1501), and a 1105 text event (t:1_2885,110:...,119:...) arrives. It is an LTP (1512) message for this member, as its web client marks it: the LTP client gets it, the Quote client nothing.

notes: 1105 carries the touchline codes 110-119 (families/xts/binary.rs parse_1105); it has no MessageCode and no trade time, so the frames carry no ltt.

The Jainam web client marks it 1512 and its adapter publishes it to every mode the symbol's subscriptions hold, the Quote one with the quantities as floats; the desktop sends an LTP message to LTP holders only (one frame per held mode from the richest message at or above it, docs/port/market-data-frames.md C08) and keeps its quote fields for the next Quote frame. The silence after the Quote client's turn is a frame the web sends and the desktop does not.

The desktop holds one subscription per instrument at the highest mode its clients ask for (websocket::manager), so the Quote client changes the LTP subscription into a Quote one; the web adapter subscribes each mode on its own.

deviations.reason: The web parses 1105 text values with float(), so in a frame from a 1105 event the quantity ltq is a double (4.0), while from a JSON event it is an integer. Number types follow the broker's web adapter (lead rule), but the dialect's floats switch is per broker, not per packet: the lead decides.

The event carries no trade time; the web sends ltt 0 (.get('LastTradedTime', 0)), the desktop leaves ltt out (docs: a field the stream does not carry is left out; never a receipt time passed off as a trade time).
